projects.title: Vincent Thomas Bridge deck replacement
projects.place: San Pedro to Terminal Island, Los Angeles
projects.summary: The Vincent Thomas Bridge carries State Route 47 across the Main Channel between San Pedro and Terminal Island, at the Port of Los Angeles. Caltrans closed the bridge to all traffic to replace its concrete deck. Caltrans says the bridge is structurally sound but the deck is deteriorating from heavy traffic and the marine environment.

facts.label: Closed to traffic
facts.note: Both directions of SR-47 between Harbor Boulevard and Ferry Street, with its on-ramps and connectors.

facts.label: Cost
facts.note: The Oct. 22 release rounds this to $750 million.

facts.label: Detour routes
facts.value: I-710, I-110, SR-103, Harry Bridges Blvd.

facts.label: Traffic control
facts.note: Local police are expanding commercial truck enforcement.

facts.label: Scope
facts.note: Also railing and fencing, center median, lighting and signs, and seismic sensors.

timeline.text: Preliminary construction began, with overnight closures in one direction at a time.
Caltrans moved the start of the full closure six days later, to Nov. 7, without changing the reopening target.
Caltrans resurfaced and restriped detour roads and intersections, installed traffic cameras, and placed temporary traffic signals.

A motion by Supervisor Janice Hahn, dated Nov. 17 and titled "Responding to the Vincent Thomas Bridge Closure," asks the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors to direct County Public Works to declare the 16-month closure a major incident, to keep evaluating recurring high-tide flooding and its effect on County storm drains, and to coordinate daily with Caltrans and the City of Los Angeles. The motion document does not record a vote.
Date by which Caltrans expects to reopen the bridge to traffic.

news.note: These reports about the detour and Los Angeles County's response are listed because they point toward public records. Reports dated Nov. 17 say the Board of Supervisors approved the motion in the timeline; the atlas has the motion's text from the County but has not yet found the Board's own record of the vote.
